title: post-upgrade compatibility scanner and shim generator
author: Hannah Liu
release_notes: Adds a post-upgrade compatibility scanner and an experimental shim generator that emits lightweight schema/runtime shims to reduce downgrade impact. No immediate user-visible changes; opt-in via installer flag.
description: Motivation: upgrades for private deployments sometimes introduce subtle incompatibilities (schema, operator CR changes, and Helm values drift) that only surface during tenant traffic. This PR implements a post-upgrade compatibility scanner that runs as part of the installer operator and an automated shim generator that produces candidate compatibility shims for quick rollback and downgrade mitigation. Design summary: 1) After an upgrade completes, the operator launches a non-blocking scanner that compares live cluster state, database schema diffs (using fast introspection), and CRD/Helm values against a compatibility policy profile for the target release. 2) The scanner reports a scored compatibility summary and writes an artifact to the release namespace with suggested shims: minimal SQL migrations or reverse-migrations, Helm value patches, and operator-side compatibility wrappers. 3) Shim artifacts are stored in an immutable release-artifacts ConfigMap and a checksum is recorded in the migration ledger; the installer offers an optional apply-shims step that can be automatically executed during rollback. 4) The shim generator is conservative: it only proposes shims that are reversible and verified by a short dry-run in a tenant-staging sandbox. Rollback safety: shims are gated by a per-tenant quarantined-apply workflow and require an explicit operator approval or an automated metric-based trigger. Linear/Jira: ENG-4123 implements scanner UI and ledger recording; ENG-4201 wires the shim dry-run harness and sandbox. Checklist: - [x] operator: post-upgrade scanner controller - [x] shim generator CLI and controller - [x] checksumed artifact storage and ledger entry - [x] dry-run harness for suggested shims - [x] installer flag: --enable-compat-shimgen (default: false) - [x] unit and integration tests covering SQL shim dry-run - [x] CI gating and e2e test in perf-canary cluster How to use: 1) Operator run: add --enable-compat-shimgen to the installer config or set installer.operator.compatShimGen.enabled=true in Helm values. 2) After upgrade, view compatibility-summary in the console or fetch release-artifact ConfigMap. 3) Review suggested shims in the UI or via redwood-privatectl shim review <release> 4) Apply shims via redwood-privatectl shim apply <release> for immediate mitigation, or include in rollback path. Testing: ran full e2e in perf-canary with a synthetic multi-tenant workload; validated shim dry-run reversibility on Postgres 13 and 14; load-tested scanner for 5000 resources with median scan duration 22s. Rollback plan: the PR is fully reversible; uninstall path removes artifacts and ledger entries. For safety, default disabled in Helm values and gate is opt-in until feature flagged for GA. Related work: references to existing snapshot-signing (pr-239874) and rollback orchestrator efforts. See linked Linear tasks for rollout and GA plan.
commits: feat(operator): add post-upgrade compat scanner controller and reconciler
feat(shimgen): implement reversible SQL/helm shim candidate generator and dry-run harness
test(shimgen): add integration tests for shim reversibility and dry-run failures
docs: document installer flag and operator UI fields
ci: add canary e2e to perf-canary workflow
review_comments: Owen Park: Can the scanner be configured to skip very large namespaces? We have clusters with tens of thousands of CRs and need an opt-out list. Author: added installer.operator.compatShimGen.namespaceExclusions and documented it in values.yaml.

Maya Patel: Please make sure the SQL shim generator never emits statements that drop columns without a corresponding reverse statement. Also request a SRE review on transaction timeouts. Author: generator now annotates shims with rollback steps and dry-run verifies rollback is idempotent; added timeout config and default 5m for dry-run transactions.

Diego Alvarez: CI failure on first run due to flaky e2e in perf-canary; reran and addressed timing by increasing test harness sleep and adding more robust readiness checks. Author: fixed and pushed, CI green.

Security review (internal): ensure shims are sanitized before being stored in ConfigMaps to avoid secrets leakage. Author: shim artifacts now scrub secrets via blocklist and use KMS-wrapped metadata for provenance.

QA: request a stronger metric to detect shim effectiveness post-apply (suggest CPU/latency regressions). Author: added post-apply metric checks and automatic rollback trigger on sustained latencies >20%.
Ops: recommend adding a migration_ledger prune policy for older artifacts. Author: added migration.ledger.pruneAfterDays with default 90 days.
Approver (Owen Park): looks good pending docs clarification about operator permissions. Author: updated docs and added an RBAC role helm chart snippet.
merge_notes: Merged after fix for e2e timing flakiness and added docs/RBAC clarifications. Feature is behind installer flag and disabled by default.
additional_context: This PR intentionally keeps the shim generator conservative: shims are suggestions that require operator approval and a dry-run sandbox verification. The goal is to reduce blast radius during rollbacks and provide actionable artifacts for rapid mitigation. Future work planned: integrate with the rollback orchestrator to auto-attach high-confidence shims during rollback plans and surface compatibility scores in the Console release timeline.
